cls: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI; R(+)-enantiomer of rabeprazole)
pharm: The R(+)-enantiomer of rabeprazole; irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) in parietal cells, suppressing basal and stimulated acid secretion.

Use only if clearly needed; limited data for this enantiomer
Avoid or use with caution; PPIs may be excreted in milk
Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment

summary: Dexrabeprazole is the R(+)-enantiomer of rabeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor marketed (mainly in India) for acid-related disorders such as gastroesophageal reflux disease, peptic ulcer, and dyspepsia. As the single active enantiomer it is given at half the racemic rabeprazole dose (10 mg) for comparable acid suppression. Like other PPIs it is taken before a meal, suppresses gastric acid by irreversibly inhibiting the parietal-cell proton pump, and shares the PPI class profile, including possible long-term risks of hypomagnesemia, vitamin B12 deficiency, Clostridioides difficile diarrhea, and fracture. Dexrabeprazole is NOT approved by the US FDA; this record is based on the parent rabeprazole label and Indian/international product information.

Duodenal ulcer and benign gastric ulcer
Helicobacter pylori eradication as part of combination therapy

dosage.n: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration

moa: Dexrabeprazole is the R(+)-enantiomer of rabeprazole. After absorption it accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculi of gastric parietal cells, where it is converted to an active sulphenamide that covalently and irreversibly binds the H+/K+-ATPase (the proton pump) - the final common step of gastric acid secretion. This blocks both basal and stimulated acid output; recovery of acid secretion requires synthesis of new pump enzyme.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to rabeprazole/dexrabeprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or any excipient
relative: Co-administration with rilpivirine or other agents requiring gastric acidity for absorption
Possible masking of gastric malignancy (investigate alarm symptoms before treating)
monitor: Symptom resolution; alarm features (weight loss, dysphagia, bleeding)

preg: There are limited data specific to the enantiomer. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not established whether dexrabeprazole is excreted in human milk; avoid use or exercise caution during breastfeeding.
renal: No dose adjustment is generally required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Exposure is increased in hepatic impairment; use with caution and monitor in severe hepatic disease.

major: Rilpivirine - PPIs substantially reduce its absorption; concomitant use is contraindicated
Atazanavir / nelfinavir - reduced absorption and loss of antiviral efficacy; avoid
moderate: Drugs whose absorption is pH-dependent (ketoconazole, itraconazole, iron salts, erlotinib) - reduced absorption
Methotrexate (high-dose) - PPIs may raise methotrexate levels
Digoxin - increased absorption with raised gastric pH
minor: Clopidogrel - class caution about reduced activation (less for rabeprazole than omeprazole)
interactions.food: Take before a meal; food can delay but not greatly reduce overall absorption.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; alcohol may aggravate reflux symptoms.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-negative urea breath tests and falsely low chromogranin A; can interfere with secretin stimulation testing.

serious: Bone fracture risk with long-term high-dose use

monitoring: Symptom resolution and need for continued therapy
Serum magnesium before and during prolonged treatment
Renal function if interstitial nephritis is suspected
counsel: Take the tablet before breakfast and swallow it whole - do not crush or chew it
Use it only for as long as your doctor advises; long-term acid suppression has risks
Tell your doctor about persistent diarrhea, muscle cramps, palpitations, or unusual tiredness
Report any difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, or unexplained weight loss
Let your doctor know about other medicines, especially HIV drugs, antifungals, or blood thinners
pk: Acid suppression begins within hours of the first dose
Plasma peak about 2-5 hours after an oral dose
Approximately 1-2 hours (acid suppression outlasts plasma levels due to irreversible binding)
Antisecretory effect persists about 24 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Store below 25-30 C; protect from light and moisture per product information
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this record is based on the parent drug rabeprazole (FDA-approved) plus Indian/international product information
Dexrabeprazole is the single R(+)-enantiomer, given at 10 mg (half the 20 mg rabeprazole dose) for comparable acid control
Take before a meal (before breakfast) for maximal proton-pump inhibition
Long-term PPI use is associated with hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency, C. difficile infection, and fracture - use lowest effective dose
Investigate alarm symptoms first; PPIs can mask gastric malignancy
missed: If you miss a dose, take it before your next meal as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not take two doses together.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited; there is no specific antidote and PPIs are highly protein bound so not readily dialyzable. Manage symptomatically and supportively.
